# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My pick: JBL Charge 6.** It's the top choice at What Hi-Fi and BestProducts, and iTechGuides calls it the best overall for beaches and pools. It's rated IP68 and lasts about 20 hours (up to 28 with Playtime Boost). It can also charge your phone. Prices in the results range from about $130 to $150, and BestProducts lists it at $150, down from $200. ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart), [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/))

## Other good options

| Need | Speaker | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Floats, even sound all around | **Ultimate Ears Epicboom** | Top pick at Tom's Guide and best mid-range at RTINGS. It's IP67, floats, has 360° sound and lasts about 15 hours. ([Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers), [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)) |
| Big pool party | **JBL Boombox 4** | RTINGS' best overall. It handles long immersion, floats, gets loud and lasts over 40 hours. Sound is directional, so it's best to face it toward listeners. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)) |
| Budget | **Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4** | It's IP67, floats and has 360° sound, with 13–14 hours of battery. It was about $65 at BestProducts. ([BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)) |
| Cheapest | **JBL Go 5** | Pocket-sized and IP67, with only 8–10 hours of battery. It was listed at $39.95. ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)) |
| Easy to carry | **JBL Grip** | Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's a can-sized IP68 speaker for about $100, with 12 hours of battery. ([Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)) |
| Loud, floating party speaker | **Soundcore Boom 2 Plus** | 100 W, IPX7, floats, and about 20 hours at half volume. It weighs 3.8 kg and is $249.99 list, or $200 with code AFSC20 per the deal site. I only found the manufacturer's specs, not an independent review. ([Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric, affiliate link](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus)) |

## Tips
- **Check the rating.** Look for IP67 or IP68 for a pool or beach. Good Housekeeping also suggests a dust rating (the first digit, IP6X) for sand. The Soundcore Boom 2 Plus has no dust rating, so keep it on a towel.
- **Rinse after use.** IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage, so rinse the speaker with fresh water, as RTINGS advises. Check your manual first, since some advise against beach or pool use.
- **Keep ports sealed and dry.** Close the charging flap before exposure and dry the speaker fully before charging.

**Buying links:** The search results didn't include direct product-page URLs, apart from the Soundcore link. Each review page linked above has current "buy" buttons for Amazon, Walmart and Best Buy, so check prices there before you order.

If you tell me your budget and whether it's just for you or for a crowd, I can narrow this to one pick.
